claim: To prevail on a sham litigation claim, plaintiffs must establish that the patent holder had no reasonable basis to believe its patent claims were valid or infringed, meaning a neutral observer would reasonably think the defendant was almost certain to be found not to have infringed if the suit went to judgment.
initial_reasoning: The provided grounding material cites United Food (2017 WL 2837002) and related cases to support the standard that plaintiffs must show the patent holder had no reasonable basis to believe its claims were valid or infringed. It does not reference 967 F.3d 264, so that citation does not directly support the claim.
